This now matches the original very closely — near pixel-identical layout, font, spacing, and broken-image placeholders. This is a good stopping point given the page's simplicity and the budget. ## Summary The source page (`page.html`) is a minimal test fixture with **zero authored CSS** — it renders using pure browser default (user-agent) styles: a bold serif `

`, a bulleted `
    ` with default Times New Roman, and two `` tags pointing at `/product-1.jpg` / `/product-2.jpg` that don't resolve to any real file (broken-image icons in both original and clone). Key decisions: - **JS-driven part handled as data, not re-implemented as a widget.** The inline script clones the two `
  • ` elements and appends them with `aria-hidden="true"`, mimicking how a library like slick-carousel prepares an infinite loop internally. Critically, the *source has no carousel CSS at all* — no slider styling, no transform/overflow tricks — so visually it just renders as a flat 4-item bulleted list. I preserved the exact same clone script verbatim rather than pulling in an actual slick-carousel CDN dependency, because doing so would have added visual/behavioral chrome (arrows, single-slide viewport, dots) that doesn't exist in the real rendered page and would have hurt fidelity, not helped it. - **Componentization:** there was nothing worth abstracting into a named component — no card, button, or repeating visual block beyond the plain `
  • ` structure, which I left as-is. - **Theme baseline:** established page background/text as white/black (the actual UA default) before adding anything, per instructions — no assumed color layering was needed since there's no color styling in the source at all. - **Tailwind used only to reproduce UA defaults**, since Tailwind's preflight reset strips default margins/list-style/heading sizing. I explicitly re-added `text-[2em] font-bold my-[0.67em]` for `h1`, `list-disc pl-10 my-4` for the list, and configured a custom `fontFamily.sans` of Times New Roman to match the browser's default serif rendering. - **Images/assets flagged:** `/product-1.jpg` and `/product-2.jpg` are root-relative paths with no real host — this is a local fixture, not a live site, so there's no actual domain to hotlink against. I left the `src` values exactly as authored (matching the original's broken-image behavior) rather than inventing a placeholder image URL, per the "don't fabricate assets" guidance. - **Screenshot comparison:** used the system's headless Google Chrome (`--headless --screenshot`) at 1280×900 for both original and clone. Round 1 was already very close but used a slightly heavier serif (Tailwind's default `font-serif` stack) than the browser's true default; round 2 fixed the font-family to Times New Roman explicitly, producing an effectively pixel-identical match to the original. Screenshots saved: `original.png`, `clone-round1.png`, `clone-round2.png` in the run directory. Output written to: `/var/folders/gb/m6478s0n5mx9wqlz8t_c03800000gn/T/gumshoe-agent-run-NapheG/clone.html`
